content.title: A Look At AeroVironment (AVAV) Valuation After Recent Share Price Pullback
content.text: AeroVironment (AVAV) has drawn attention after a sharp pullback, with the stock showing a negative return over the past month and past 3 months. This has prompted investors to reassess expectations around its valuation. See our latest analysis for AeroVironment. The recent pullback sits against a much stronger longer term picture, with a 1 year total shareholder return of 58.16% and a 3 year total shareholder return of 119.54%. Short term share price momentum is clearly fading, while longer term holders have still seen substantial gains. If AeroVironment’s recent swings have you thinking about other opportunities in the robotics and automation space, this is a good moment to scan 32 robotics and automation stocks So with AVAV pulling back in the short term but still posting strong multi year shareholder returns and trading at a discount to analyst targets, is this a fresh entry point, or is the market already pricing in future growth? Most Popular Narrative: 31.1% Undervalued Vestra’s fair value estimate of $287 for AeroVironment sits well above the last close at $197.72, which is why the narrative frames AVAV as an undervalued story with a long runway tied to execution and integration. The core of the AVAV thesis lies in its "High-Margin Manufacturing Shift." Historically viewed as an R&D-heavy boutique firm, AeroVironment is transforming into a high-volume producer of "consumable" defense tech. The Switchblade has become the "Stinger missile of the 21st century," and the transition to the Block 2 variant, which offers better ATR (Automatic Target Recognition) and resilience in GPS-denied environments, is driving higher unit prices. While the current P/E ratio remains elevated near 80x to 90x due to non-cash merger charges, the market is beginning to price AVAV as a core "Sovereign Defense" play. The primary risk remains the "lumpiness" of government contracts, but the record $1.1 billion backlog provides a significant cushion for the quarters ahead. Read the complete narrative. Want to see what sits behind that $287 figure? The narrative leans heavily on a step change in scale, richer margins, and a future earnings profile that is closer to established defense leaders than a niche drone supplier. Curious which revenue mix, backlog conversion, and profit assumptions are doing the heavy lifting here? The full narrative lays out those moving parts in detail. Result: Fair Value of $287 (UNDERVALUED) Have a read of the narrative in full and understand what's behind the forecasts. However, this hinges on government contract timing and BlueHalo integration remaining on track, with any delays or cost surprises quickly challenging the current growth-focused story. Find out about the key risks to this AeroVironment narrative. Another View: Our DCF Model Sees Limited Upside Vestra’s fair value of $287 paints AeroVironment as undervalued, but the SWS DCF model points the other way. On that view, AVAV’s future cash flows line up closer to $153.29 per share, which would make the current $197.72 price look expensive rather than cheap. So which story do you lean toward?
